title: Forks
summary: Learn how one move can attack two targets.

steps.title: One move, two targets
steps.body: A fork is a move that attacks two pieces at once. The opponent can usually save only one. Knights are famous for forks because their L-shaped jump is hard to see.

steps.title: A knight fork
steps.body: The knight on c7 attacks the king on a8 and the rook on e8 at the same time.

steps.title: Fork the king and queen
steps.body: Move the knight from d4 to f5. It will check the king and attack the queen.
steps.successText: f5 attacks g7 and e3. That is a fork.
steps.errorText: Jump the knight from d4 to f5.

steps.title: A pawn fork
steps.body: Push the pawn from d2 to d4. From d4 it attacks both black knights.
steps.successText: Pawns fork on the two squares they attack diagonally.
steps.errorText: Advance the d2 pawn two squares to d4.

steps.title: Spot the idea
steps.question: What makes a fork powerful?

choices.label: It attacks two things, so one can be won
It lets a pawn move backward

steps.successText: Look for one piece that can attack two undefended or valuable targets.
steps.errorText: A fork is about two targets, not an automatic mate.

steps.title: Lesson recap
steps.body: Before you move, ask: does my opponent have a fork? After you move, ask the same question about your own pieces.
